body.x: inDJ (CEO Woo-ju Jung) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

Established in 2019, inDJ is a company that researches and develops platforms that provide AI-based music recommendation services. The main point of the platform is to analyze over 20,000 personalized situations in real-time with AI and to provide music and content befitting those situations. It is further differentiated by its characteristic ability to provide music recommendations based on the user’s mood patterns.

In addition to simply recommending the user’s preferred music genre, their music recommendation platform’s AI analyzes the user’s mood, the weather, and behavioral patterns, based on smartphones, IoT, and connected car sensors, to derive recommendation results. In addition, they are able to analyze the moods of each song, instrument composition, BPM (Beats Per Minute), and social network (SNS) data through an AI labeling system to make their recommendations, improving the accuracy of their recommendations.

Through such services, inDJ recorded sales totaling 430 million KRW last year and 500 million KRW by the 2nd quarter of this year in the Korean market. It has been said that they are expecting over 1 billion KRW in sales by the end of 2022. After proving their excellent business feasibility in the market, they are now collaborating and conducting PoC with Korean university hospitals, patients with mental illnesses, and various autonomous car related companies to advance their technology.

An official of inDJ revealed their reason for participation, saying, “We plan on promoting our music platform service and our situation and mood analysis AI to search for buyers and investors that are suitable for the current stage,” and said, “In addition, we are also focusing on having close meetings with healthcare and autonomous car service companies to promote collaborations and new businesses.”

Furthermore, they are preparing to create new community services that integrate the foundation of their services and the K-Pop trend, which is currently prevalent in the global content market. An official of inDJ said that, “Considering the situation of specialized communities for global K-Pop fans not being built properly yet, we plan to provide services for their fandoms,” and said that, “This will be a combination of technologies and content representing the 4th industrial revolution, with things like the metaverse and NFT.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
